civilopediaText.text: The army's headquarters, with its staff, signals and guard. Losing it means losing the army: in the D-Day scenario, capturing the German headquarters at Saint-Lô wins a Breakout victory.
It is far stronger than any other city: taking it needs a deliberate assault with artillery and several regiments. The Allied headquarters is aboard ship, out of reach of the German army.

Unbuildable
Unsellable

civilopediaText.text: One of the 13 key positions of the D-Day scenario: Utah Beach, Sainte-Mère-Église, Carentan, Pointe du Hoc, Omaha Beach, Port-en-Bessin, Gold Beach, Bayeux, Juno Beach, Carpiquet, Caen, Sword Beach and Pegasus Bridge.

Each is a city that cannot be razed. Sainte-Mère-Église and Pegasus Bridge start in Allied hands - taken by the airborne in the night; the rest are held by the Germans. At the end of turn 38 (9 PM, June 8) the Allies win Hold the Beachhead if they hold at least 10 key positions; otherwise Germany wins Contain the Invasion.

name: Beach Defenses
uniques: Normandy Scenario
Unbuildable
Unsellable
Never destroyed when the city is captured
Removes extra unhappiness from annexed cities

civilopediaText.text: A Widerstandsnest of the Atlantic Wall: concrete bunkers and casemates, machine-gun nests, a 50mm or 75mm gun sited to fire along the beach, trenches, wire and mines - and, below the high-water mark, thousands of steel hedgehogs, stakes and ramps, many topped with mines.

The five beaches - Utah Beach, Omaha Beach, Gold Beach, Juno Beach and Sword Beach - are key positions. Once the Allies hold a beach, its follow-up waves come ashore there instead of landing from the sea. If the Germans hold all five at the end of any turn from turn 10 (4 PM, June 6) onward, they win the Into the Sea victory.

civilopediaText.text: An assault force anchored in the Transport Area, eleven miles out: transports, landing ships, the headquarters ship and the bombarding warships.

Follow-up waves are lowered into their landing craft here and appear embarked beside it at the start of their turn. Landing craft move 5 tiles; landing on a beach takes the rest of the turn (Rangers, Commandos and DD tanks land without stopping). Once ashore, troops cannot re-embark.
